description: This is a false-colour satellite or aerial image displaying a wide, braided river system with multiple channels and extensive floodplains. The water bodies, including the main river channels and smaller water courses, are depicted in a bright turquoise/cyan colour. Densely vegetated areas, such as forests or agricultural fields on the surrounding land and some larger islands, appear in various shades of red and magenta, characteristic of False Colour Infrared (FCIR) imagery where healthy vegetation reflects strongly in the near-infrared spectrum. Areas within the floodplain and on some islands, which likely represent sand and gravel deposits, alluvial fans, or areas with sparse vegetation, are shown in lighter pink and white tones. A small green circular marker is visible on a vegetated island located within the main river's upper central channel. The image illustrates features relevant to the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) for identifying river banks and dry river beds as defined in land cover mapping guidelines.
